text:
maria: quick heads-up, my docs PR (RFC + examples) is green in CI but blocked on a runtime confirmation. I changed the SDK docs to say the default for streaming is off for small payloads. Can runtime confirm: does the API still send a final 'end_of_stream' event when streaming=false? :eyes:

kevin: I skimmed the PR — can you paste the exact wording you added? want to make sure we don't break existing customers relying on stream termination events.

maria: sure — I added this example and wording:

```yaml
# example client config in docs
client:
  streaming: false  # default for lightweight clients
  prefer_latency: true
  fallback_to_sync: true
```

And in the prose: "When streaming is false the SDK will use a synchronous response; if a model variant only supports streaming the service will automatically convert to a synchronous final payload."

samira: that last sentence is what I flagged in the PR comments. Is the automatic conversion guaranteed? If not we should hedge the language.

runtime-eng: short answer: we do not emit streaming events when streaming=false. There is no "end_of_stream" event in that path. For compatibility we do offer an automatic fallback to a sync response payload for some models, but it is not universal — depends on model runtime capability and the route config.

runtime-eng: more details: the routing layer will try to translate streaming-only model output into a single final message when the request header `X-Client-Streaming: false` is present, but only if the model adapter implements aggregation. If aggregation isn't available you'll get a 422 with header `X-Requires-Streaming: true`.

kevin: ah ok — so docs wording should call out both behaviors and the 422 edge case. Maybe add the header names and the expected status.

maria: got it. what exact phrasing would you recommend? I want something concise for the quickstart and a more detailed note below.

runtime-eng: suggested short text to use in quickstart:

"By default the SDK uses synchronous responses (streaming: false). If a model can only produce streamed outputs, the platform will attempt to aggregate into a final response. If aggregation is not supported, the request will fail with 422 and the response will include header `X-Requires-Streaming: true`. For streaming behavior, set `streaming: true` in client config."

maria: perfect. I'll swap that in. Also updating the examples.

docs-bot: docs preview available: https://preview.redwood.ai/docs/pr/892 — CI artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/892/artifacts 

kevin: one more tiny ask — can you add the exact fallback header name in the SDK snippet so engineers can detect and surface a helpful error in their apps?

maria: added snippet with check for header in the error handling example. Pushing new commit now.

samira: thanks — once that wording and snippet land, I'm happy to approve. :thumbsup:

maria: pushing now. last_message: ping me if CI preview link updates and I'll re-check.
